ingrid_support: Hey team — hitting a weird rerank behavior. We send a top-level "query" and each document also contains a "query" field (legacy). Response rates 200 but some candidates get score 0 or ordering looks like it's using per-doc queries instead of the top-level one. Repro below, minimal payload and response snippet. Anyone seen this?

ingrid_support: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/rerank \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "query": "what is refund policy",
    "documents": [
      {"id":"d1","text":"refund policy for plan A","query":"refund plan"},
      {"id":"d2","text":"how to cancel subscription","query":"cancel subscription"}
    ],
    "candidates": ["d1","d2"]
  }'
```

ingrid_support: response (trimmed): ```json
{
  "ranked_candidates": [
    {"id":"d2","score":0.0},
    {"id":"d1","score":0.0}
  ]
}```

matt_dev: thanks, this looks like a name-collision issue. If you include a field named "query" inside documents we currently flatten some nested keys server-side which can cause the request parser to prefer the inner value in some code paths. Not intended behavior.

ingrid_support: interesting — when we changed inner key to "doc_query" everything ranked normally.

kevin_se: quick workaround: rename any per-document "query" to something else (doc_query or metadata.query). We treat top-level "query" as the rerank query. We'll push a fix to stop flattening.

sophie_cs: is this causing 422s for some users too? we had a customer hit a 422 when they had nested "passages" inside "documents" and also a top-level "candidates" array.

matt_dev: the 422 is a separate validation edge-case: if you send documents with nested arrays named "passages" and also pass candidates by id, our validation sometimes tries to validate the candidate payload shape against the passage shape and rejects when lengths mismatch. If you can reproduce, please include a minimal curl like above and the server error body.

ingrid_support: pasted the 422 body earlier in the ticket — it complained about "passages: expected array of strings" but we submitted objects. Looks like docs/examples diverge.

carla_docs: noted. I'll update the docs with two minimal recommended schemas: (a) simple candidates-by-id + top-level query, (b) per-document passages where candidates are inline objects. Also add a callout: avoid naming inner fields "query".

support-bot: Created INC-9147 and linked to INF-9123 (rerank flattening bug). Assigned to eng-runtime.

kevin_se: timeline: we'll ship a patch to stop the problematic flattening within 48 hours. In the meantime please use the rename workaround or move per-doc subfields under a "metadata" object. Example safe payload:```json
{
  "query":"what is refund policy",
  "documents":[{"id":"d1","text":"refund policy","metadata":{"doc_query":"refund plan"}}],
  "candidates":["d1"]
}```

ingrid_support: confirmed — rename -> metadata fix works for our customer. Closing the escalated ticket after they validate. Thanks all :thumbsup:

matt_dev: follow-up: we'll also add a lint rule in the SDK to warn when a document contains a "query" key to prevent new users from tripping this.

carla_docs: adding a short note to the rerank quickstart and an example repro + fix.

sophie_cs: great. marking this thread resolved on our side; will reopen if the customer sees more anomalies.
